threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it the 'Overground,' but the locals just say 'the train' like they're back in the 70s. Makes you stand out real quick.
Caught the 35 last night, a guy was trying to impress a girl with magic tricks but kept dropping the cards. She seemed more interested in her phone.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift soccer goal in a graffiti-tagged alley, using old crates and a bicycle tire. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a döner shop with a beer garden that doubles as a gallery space—art and kebab culture collide like nowhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can name the taco truck that’s been at 24th and Mission longer than the coffee shop has.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 at Civic Center today, drivers having to coax a dog off the tracks. Only in SF do you see pets holding up public transport.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all barcelona's life happens on the Rambla. Meanwhile, Gràcia's plazas are alive at night with locals and their kids running wild.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they pause at every street corner, reading their map like it’s an ancient treasure map rather than just streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of just 'the train' like everyone else round here. It's a dead giveaway.
Last night on the 59, a woman in a fur coat was arguing about the price of avocados. The bus driver just kept nodding, clearly used to it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a toddler arguing with their mom in Arabic while a cat lounged on the sidewalk, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a café where you can sip coffee while watching a street artist paint a mural just across the road. Real Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals will know to avoid 16th and Mission during rush hour—it's a gamble with buses, skateboards, and the occasional dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit calmly reading a newspaper while the bus was inching along during a protest. Only in SF can you be late and composed at the same time.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Many tourists think Gràcia is just a party zone, but they miss the tiny local bakeries that open at 6 AM and sell the best ensaïmades.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot them by the way they order a 'café con leche' without knowing it’s mostly milk here. Look for the puzzled faces.
